review_rows.justification:
The observation is correct. However, NIA followed the existing layout of the National Expenditure Program (NEP), which is why the three (3) projects remain listed in the last portion of the Establishment of Pump Irrigation Projects.

Should the repositioning of these projects within the NEP annex be allowed, the following projects should be properly placed under Region II (Cagayan Valley), specifically under their respective provinces:

1.        Mamil Pump Irrigation Project – Cagayan
2.        Santa Maria Pump Irrigation Project – Isabela
3.        Catugan Pump Irrigation Project – Cagayan

In this regard, may we respectfully request the correction of the placement of the Santa Maria Pump Irrigation Project under the Province of Isabela, while the Mamil and Catugan Pump Irrigation Projects shall be placed under the Province of Cagayan.

The geographical coordinates have been verified and confirmed based on the approved design and Civil 3D data.

workbook.submission_label: Rehabilitation and Protection of Watershed Management
workbook.justification: On August 5, 2019, the National Irrigation Administration (NIA) and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) signed a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) to strengthen the sustainable management, protection, development, and rehabilitation of 143 watersheds supporting National Irrigation Systems (NIS) nationwide. Pursuant to DENR Memorandum Circular No. 2008-05, the agreement establishes the respective responsibilities of both agencies in preparing Integrated Watershed Management Plans (IWMPs), identifying priority watersheds for rehabilitation, securing environmental clearances, enforcing forestry laws, conducting research and information campaigns, and mobilizing funding resources. The partnership adopts an integrated watershed ecosystem management approach to ensure the long-term sustainability of irrigation systems while promoting environmental conservation and effective watershed management.

coordinate_workbook.revised_title: Ambayoan RIS: Repair of Damaged Canal Lining along the Ambayoan River Irrigation System Main Canal (Sta. 4+480–Sta. 4+639.5)
coordinate_workbook.justification:
The changes were made due to ongoing construction works covering Sta. 3+901 to Sta. 4+480, which are being implemented in two phases: Phase 1 (Sta. 4+155 to Sta. 4+480) and Phase 2 (Sta. 3+901 to Sta. 4+155).

The adjustment in project stationing to Sta. 4+480–Sta. 4+639.5 is necessary to prevent duplication of scope and ensure optimal fund utilization. Due to the severe impacts of the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) this year, an emergency fund was allocated to address critical damages along the Main Canal, which already covers the previously proposed station as an ongoing project. Shifting the station limits redirects the proposed repair works to an adjacent, unprogrammed, and severely damaged section of the Main Canal that requires immediate rehabilitation to maintain uninterrupted irrigation water delivery.

coordinate_workbook.justification: The realignment of the proposed project from Lateral AF to Lateral BF (Sta. 0+224–Sta. 0+991) is necessary to prioritize the more severely damaged canal section and optimize resource allocation. Following joint field validation and condition assessment of the system, it was determined that Lateral BF exhibits severe structural deterioration requiring immediate intervention compared to Lateral AF, which remains functional. Reallocating the project scope to Lateral BF ensures that critical conveyance issues are addressed promptly to prevent severe water losses and maintain efficient irrigation delivery to downstream service areas.

coordinate_workbook.revised_title: Ngayaongaoan CIS: Repair of Canal Lining (Sta. 0+912–Sta. 1+202
coordinate_workbook.justification:
The adjustment in project stationing to Sta. 0+912–Sta. 1+202 is requested to prioritize the most severely damaged portion of the canal system and align with the immediate operational needs of the Irrigators Association (IA).
Following joint field validation with the IA, it was determined that while the previously proposed section sustained only minor typhoon-related damages, the downstream stretch at Sta. 0+912–Sta. 1+202 remains unlined and exhibits severe structural deterioration. Realigning the project scope to address this critical, unlined, and severely damaged segment is essential to minimize significant conveyance and seepage losses, ensuring uninterrupted irrigation water delivery to the tail-end service areas.

coordinate_workbook.revised_title: Estanza CIS: Restoration of Canal Lining (Sta. 0+570–Sta. 1+128)
coordinate_workbook.justification:
The adjustment in project stationing to Sta. 0+570–Sta. 1+128 is necessary to address an urgent structural failure along the canal.
The canal lining within this newly proposed section has already collapsed, causing severe seepage and significant wastage of irrigation water. This water loss has directly resulted in an inadequate supply reaching the downstream service areas, particularly at the tail end of the system. Prioritizing this critical section over the previously proposed station is essential to prevent further structural deterioration, minimize conveyance losses, and restore equitable water distribution to affected farmers.

workbook.justification: Considering that the entire Allay-Nangcalapan CIS is currently non-operational, it is necessary to prioritize its rehabilitation and restoration through the consolidation of available RESTO-CIS funds from two separate projects into a single project allocation. While the consolidated budget remains insufficient to fully restore the irrigation system, the proposed consolidation will enable the implementation of more substantial and strategically prioritized rehabilitation works, optimize the utilization of limited financial resources, and maximize the effectiveness and impact of the proposed interventions. This approach is intended to facilitate the progressive restoration of the system's operational functionality and ultimately restore irrigation services to its intended farmer-beneficiaries.

coordinate_workbook.justification:
During the construction of the Licaray Pump Irrigation System (PIS), it was established that the project site was originally identified as being within the territorial jurisdiction of Barangay Quezon. Where Licaray Creek serves as the natural boundary between the two neighboring barangays, namely Barangay Quezon and Barangay Doña Paulina.

However pursuant to a Sangguniang Barangay Resolution issued by Barangay Victoria (formerly named as Barangay Doña Paulina), the Licaray PIS was declared to be within the territorial jurisdiction of Barangay Victoria.

workbook.justification: Based on the latest assessment of the project area, the installation of a solar-powered groundwater pumping system is deemed necessary to supplement the existing water supply, considering its location at the tail-end of the irrigation system and the continuous reduction in water availability from the existing source. Hence, the project scope is proposed to include the construction of a solar-powered pump system in addition to canal lining to ensure a more reliable and sustainable water supply and improve irrigation service delivery to the intended beneficiaries.
